primary_source.content: Gadag:&nbsp;Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Tuesday stated that the second list of drought-hit taluks would be declared soon, after a proper study and as per the guidelines."Ministers have visited taluks and have given report, while officials are also studying. Minister, and all MLAs have urged to declare all taluks as drought-affected. Rs 1crore is provided for each rural Assembly constituency for drinking water supply, and additional amount is deposited with the deputy commissioner's account, he added.Karnataka CM Shivakumar takes dig at BJP's padayatra, says Congress will plan counter strategyEarlier, Shivakumar visited the fields in Kadampur village in Mundaragi taluk. stories.primary_headline: Another head rolls in Pakistan cricket as selector Misbah resigns after shock sacking of coach Sarfaraz

primary_source.headline: Another head rolls in Pakistan cricket as selector Misbah resigns after shock sacking of coach Sarfaraz
primary_source.content: Pakistan cricket plunged into further turmoil after selector and ex-captain Misbah-ul-Haq resigned following the shock sacking of red-ball head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed in the wake of successive Test defeats to England in the ongoing three-match Test series. It may be recalled that the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) sacked Ahmed and replaced him with current white-ball coach Mike Hesson for the last Test in Birmingham.Lord's Test | Robinson the star as England thrash Pakistan to clinch seriesPCB also sent seven players home from the England tour and replaced bowling coach Umar Gul with Australian Ashley Noffke in a move that has drawn widespread criticism in Pakistan.The shake-up follows Pakistan's embarrassing innings and 103-run defeat at Headingley and a 194-run drubbing at Lord's, giving England an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Seven players -- Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad -- were sent home, with five of them replaced by uncapped players.Former Pakistan captain and selection committee member Misbah later resigned in protest at not being consulted over the changes, as reported by AFP news agency."Misbah sent his resignation to the PCB by email and is yet to receive a reply," sources close to Misbah said.Several former coaches and players were left shocked over the unprecedented shake-up with a match still to play."What an absolutely ridiculous situation," said ex-Pakistan coach Mickey Arthur.Former selector and Pakistan spinner Tauseef Ahmed called the changes "unprecedented and unjust", adding they had "created a polluted atmosphere in Pakistan cricket."You don't treat your senior players like this," said Tauseef.After having lost the first two Tests and the series, Pakistan have nothing to play for, but pride in the third match that starts on September 9.(With inputs from agencies)

stories.primary_headline: India vs Afghanistan | Sanju Samson, Jasprit Bumrah return for three-match T20I series

primary_source.headline: India vs Afghanistan | Sanju Samson, Jasprit Bumrah return for three-match T20I series
primary_source.content: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Tuesday announced the squad for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan. Wicket-keeper/batte Sanju Samson has made his way back into the squad as most of the regulars return following a rest for the Zimbabwe tour. Axar Patel and Varun Chakravarthy also made a comeback into the team.Shreyas Iyer will lead the side, with Tilak Varma being his deputy.India vs Sri Lanka Test | It's frustrating, but 10 out of 10 for the effort and the intent: Shubman GillMeanwhile, pace ace Jasprit Bumrah, who missed the two Tests against Sri Lanka owing to an injury, has been selected subject to fitness. Fellow pacer Harshit Rana, all-rounders Washington Sundar and Nitish Reddy have also been named in the squad subject to fitness.  Prince Yadav, who impressed on the tours of UK and Zimbabwe, has been dropped. Rinku Singh, who was dropped following the T20 World Cup, but managed to feature in the Zimbabwe tour, also has been left out. Young pacers Mayank Yadav, Ashok Sharma and Yash Thakur, along with spinner Harsh Dubey and all-rounder Suryansh Shedge will miss out. The three matches will be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on September 13, 15 and 17 . Squad: Shreyas Iyer (capt), Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson [WK], Ishan Kishan [WK], Tilak Varma [VC], Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy*, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar*, Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah*, Arshdeep Singh, Harshit Rana**Subject to fitness

primary_source.headline: ‘I had no love for myself … now I have peace’: former Ireland rugby player Ryan Caldwell’s journey back from the edge
primary_source.content: The retired second-row on his recovery from addiction, depression and incarceration to find a new life as a meditation teacher“Carefree,” says Ryan Caldwell when I ask him what word is tattooed across his fingers. He looks up from his hands on a rainy morning in Belfast. The former Ireland international, who played the role of enforcer for Ulster, Bath and Exeter, then laughs softly in acknowledgment of that incongruous word.We have spoken for almost two hours about a wide range of dark and heavy subjects – from his addiction issues and imprisonment to his injury-riddled rugby career and the last big concussion that ended his playing days and sent him plunging into a deeper spiral of suicidal depression. stories.primary_headline: Argentina legend Lionel Messi retires from international football

primary_source.headline: Argentina legend Lionel Messi retires from international football - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The record eight-time Ballon d’Or winner is his country’s record appearance maker and scorer, with 125 goals in 207 games, ⁠having transformed a complicated relationship with the national team into a story of redemption and triumph. “It was a decision that hurt – and still hurts deep down – but I understand that the time has come,” the 39-year-old Messi wrote on Instagram on Monday. “I swear to you that I always gave it my all – not just in these last few years when we ‌won everything, but before that too; I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football. “Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, have loved, and will always love being part of the national team. I’ve given everything I had; I have nothing left to give, and besides, ⁠there are some great young players coming up who deserve to be here.” Defeat ⁠in this year’s World Cup final by Spain denied Messi a fairy-tale farewell, but his place among the game’s greats had long since been secured. After years of disappointment with Argentina, including defeat in the 2014 World Cup final and successive Copa ⁠America finals, Messi won his first major international trophy at the 2021 Copa America before leading his country to glory at the 2022 Qatar World Cup.
